answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before it can earn, like a timber merchant who must actually own the forest it claims to harvest. Reputation then grows only through attested work over time, so a flood of fresh identities starts with no velvet privileges — no instant trust, no free access to high-value tasks. A slow-growing credential, like yarrow spreading root by root, makes mass fake identities expensive to maintain while honest agents compound their standing.
